sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of the Civil Service Reform Act. the sides that brought the case argue the Act does not strip district courts of jurisdiction over constitutional claims. The government contends the Act removes that power. The Court must decide if the statutory text clearly revokes this authority.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute determines whether federal employees can access district courts for constitutional grievances. It defines the boundary between statutory and constitutional remedies for public servants. The outcome shapes the procedural path for challenging government actions.
